name: Lesotho
snapshot: A mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, dependent on water exports and textile jobs that were hit by US tariffs in 2025.
culture: Lesotho's entire territory lies above 1,000 metres, earning it the name "kingdom in the sky". The Basotho blanket, worn as a cloak, and the conical mokorotlo hat are national symbols that appear on the flag. Sesotho is spoken by nearly everyone. Famo music, sung by migrant miners with accordions, is tied to rivalries that have sometimes turned violent.
society: Generations of Basotho men worked in South African mines. Today textiles for US brands and water sold to South Africa through the Lesotho Highlands Water Project are key earners. Lesotho has one of the world's highest HIV rates. Politics has been unstable, with frequent coalition collapses and army interventions.
situation: Sam Matekane, a mining tycoon, became prime minister in 2022 at the head of his new Revolution for Prosperity party. Lesotho was singled out for a 50 percent tariff in Trump's April 2025 announcements; the rate was later cut, but factory orders and thousands of textile jobs had already been lost, and duty-free access to the US market remains uncertain. King Letsie III is the ceremonial head of state.
power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. The prime minister leads the majority in the 120-seat National Assembly, elected by mixed-member proportional representation; the Senate includes the principal chiefs. The army has intervened in politics several times.
